clips.send: Common mix-up: Cai Lun improved papermaking; he did not invent it (paper already existed in the Western Han dynasty). Bi Sheng invented movable-type printing; woodblock printing already existed in the Tang dynasty. The sinan spoon is from the Warring States period; the compass went to sea in the Northern Song dynasty.

clips.send: What do a dollar bill, a library book, the compass app on a phone and Fourth of July fireworks have in common? Each one goes back to something first made in China: paper, printing, the compass and gunpowder. Chinese textbooks call them the Four Great Inventions (四大发明, sì dà fāmíng). They reached Europe through Arab traders, centuries before there was a United States.

clips.send: Making a sheet of paper. Pulp, screen, dry, peel. one, Soak and cut the raw materials. two, Pound them into pulp. three, Dip a bamboo screen into the pulp vat and lift out a thin wet layer. four, Press and dry the sheets. five, Peel off the finished paper. Paper replaced heavy bamboo slips and expensive silk as the main writing material. Papermaking later spread to Korea, Japan and the Arab world, and then to Europe through the Arabs. Drag the Papermaking slider through steps 1–5!

clips.send: 一张纸币、一本图书、手机里的指南针、节日的烟花，有什么共同点？它们都可以追溯到中国古代的发明。造纸术、印刷术、指南针和火药是中国古代劳动人民的伟大创造，它们经阿拉伯人传到欧洲，深刻改变了世界。拨一拨司南，做一张纸，再亲手用活字印一个词！然后拖动年份滑块，看每项发明怎样一步步传向西方。
